claims.text: A need is a good or service a person must have to survive, such as food, water and shelter; a want is a good or service a person would like to have but can survive without.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Scarcity is the situation in which the resources available to satisfy needs and wants are limited, so choices have to be made about how they are used.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: The opportunity cost of a choice is the next-best alternative given up when that choice is made.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Specialisation is when a worker, a business or a country concentrates on producing a limited range of goods or services instead of trying to produce everything for itself.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Specialisation tends to raise output per worker because steady practice at one narrow task builds speed and skill, which is why businesses often divide work between specialists.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Specialisation carries costs alongside its benefits: narrow repetitive work can lower motivation, and a business can become dependent on a few specialists who are hard to replace.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: The purpose of business activity is to organise scarce resources to produce the goods and services that satisfy people's needs and wants, and to exchange that output for money.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Because specialised producers each make a narrow range of products and exchange them through trade, people are able to consume far more goods and services than they could make for themselves.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Added value is the difference between the selling price of a product and the cost of the bought-in materials and other inputs used to make it.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: A business can increase its added value either by raising the price customers are willing to pay, through quality, branding, design or convenience, or by reducing the cost of the bought-in materials and inputs.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.

claims.text: Added value and profit are different measures: added value is the gap between selling price and bought-in input costs, while profit is what remains after every business cost, including wages, rent and transport, has been paid.

verification.method: Authored originally against the 0450 v2 syllabus scope under standard v0.2.0-draft. Requires independent semantic review (RS-28) before publication.
